Download

Thanks for downloading Clipsa

Clipsa 0.1.4 for Linux (Clipsa_0.1.4_amd64.deb) is downloading from GitHub Releases. If nothing happens, use the button below.

Download again What's new in 0.1.4

Also for Linux: .rpm (Fedora, openSUSE) · AppImage (any distribution) · all files on GitHub

Install

Three steps to your first paste

  1. 1

    Install the package

    From the folder you downloaded to, run:
    sudo apt install ./Clipsa_0.1.4_amd64.deb
  2. 2

    Start Clipsa

    Open Clipsa from your applications menu. Clipsa stores its key in the Secret Service, so GNOME Keyring, KWallet or another provider must be running. It keeps running in the tray when you close its window; on GNOME, tray icons need the AppIndicator extension, which Ubuntu includes.
  3. 3

    Open the picker

    The welcome screen asks whether Clipsa may check for updates. Then press Ctrl Shift V in any app to open the quick picker, and Enter to paste. Linux can't tell Clipsa which copies are secret, so use Pause monitoring in the tray before copying passwords.

Verify

Check what you downloaded

Every installer is built by Clipsa's public release workflow and published with a SHA256SUMS file on the GitHub release. To compare your download with it:

cd ~/Downloads
curl -LO https://github.com/mordamax/clipsa/releases/download/v0.1.4/SHA256SUMS
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS

It prints Clipsa_0.1.4_amd64.deb: OK when the file matches. The same SHA-256 is listed next to each file on the release page.
